newsitem.title: LEBANON: Plastic waste leaves Beirut back to Germany.
newsitem.headline: Plastic waste leaves Beirut back to Germany.

text.p: A ship carrying the first batch of 36 containers of plastic waste illegally imported to Lebanon last August left Beirut on Tuesday on its way back to Germany.
Belgian carrier Ahlers Belgica loaded with 21 containers of the contaminated waste left the port under the observation of Lebanese officials and German diplomats.

"The containers are finally leaving the same way they came," German embassy Counselor Wolfgang Lerke told reporters at Beirut port. "The 21 containers will arrive in Germany in two weeks and the other 15 will be shipped in two weeks time".
The international environmental watchdog Greenpeace last October helped uncover the scandal. Lebanese experts said it was polluted plastic waste and toxic chemicals that endangered public health.

In February a Lebanese magistrate demanded up to 10 years in jail for three Lebanese men in connection with the shipment made by German firms International Trade and Finance in Saulheim and RC Reifenrecycling in Hagen.
Lebanon held the shipment at the port and began campaigning to have Germany take back all 680 tonnes.
Lerke said Ahlers Belgica would make stops in Latakia port in Syria and Gioia Tauro port in Italy before reaching Bremer Haven port in Germany.
"None of the containers will be lost on the way and all of them will be destroyed in Germany," Lerke added.

Greenpeace Mediterranean campaigner in Beirut Fouad Hamdan was at the port: "Lebanon is today sending a clear warning to all waste traders world-wide. It is telling them that any waste entering Lebanon will be returned to sender at the expenses of the exporting company or government."
Lerke said a fund set up by German industry and supervised by the Bonn government was financing the shipment and incineration. This was the first operation to be handled by the fund, he said.
"Shipping and destroying these wastes will cost a couple of thousands U.S. dollars, and it will be covered by German Solidarity Fund," he said.
